pr_title: Warn when `WindowDescriptor` is inserted after adding `WindowPlugin`.
pr_body:
# Objective

Warn the user when `WindowDescriptor` is inserted after adding the `WindowPlugin`.
As a bonus, panic when trying to access `WindowDescriptor` in a system.
Fixes #5884.

# Migration Guide
The `WindowDescriptor` resource is now removed after the `WindowPlugin` is added.
Use the `Windows` resource to edit or read info from the primary window.
```rust
fn system(windows: Res<Windows>) {
    let window = windows.primary();
}
```

`#[cfg(debug_assertions)]` is the way to add assertions that you don't want to pay the cost of in release builds.
What alternative is there?

The alternative here is to enforce this behavior more robustly as a class, using #2988. This is my (fairly strong) preference here.

This is a real problem, but I think we can introduce good systematic tools.

Sorry, I wasn't being very clear.
This PR is a band-aid to make people using `WindowDescriptor` less prone to shooting themselves in the foot. I very much look forward to a better solution, but that looks like its going to take a while yet.

I was asking whether there's an alternative to using `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]` that Francois would like.
The only alternative I see is to just have it always run.
Adding the Controversial label here. #2988 is scheduled to be merged on October 21, and I much prefer that solution.

issue_context.title: Add a warning if `WindowDescriptor` is inserted after the render plugin
issue_context.body:
## How can Bevy's documentation be improved?

To set the `present_mode` (aka vsync) of the bevy app, it is required that the `WindowDescriptor`  resource be inserted before the insertion of the core bevy rendering plugin, so that it's possible to set the present mode when initializing rendering-related resources.

It is easy to mistakenly add the `WindowDescriptor` **after** the default bevy plugins. And there is absolutely no feedback telling user that they are "holding it wrong," resulting in difficult-to-understand unexpected behavior.

There should be a check on whether `WindowDescriptor` was inserted/updated after its useful insertion time and print a warning, explaining what problems this entails and how to fix the issue (adding the resource _before_ the rendering plugin).
comments: This PR would solve this more generally instead of being WindowDescriptor specific https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/pull/2988

review_comments: This might be breaking if somehow some users rely on that `WindowDescriptor` resource. Though I don't see a usecase where that is needed.

Using `WindowDescriptor` as a source of information about the window is also a bit of a footgun.
I'll add a migration guide :+1:
